newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's ailing Tudjman urges rebel Serbs to vote.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's ailing Tudjman urges rebel Serbs to vote.

text.p: Ailing Croatian President Franjo Tudjman said on Tuesday that minority Serbs in their last rebel enclave should fully participate in a local March election to complete Eastern Slavonia's return to Croatian rule.

"From this place I call upon all the Serbs (in Eastern Slavonia) to take part in the voting for local administrative bodies," the 74-year old president, said to be ill with cancer, told the parliament in his annual "state of the nation" speech.

Of some 120,000 Serbs currently in the region, about half are refugees. Zagreb has allowed them to vote in March 16 election for the areas where they lived before their 1991 rebellion against Croatia's secession from Yugoslavia.
Tudjman said some militant Serbs were still resisting the region's reintegration and were "making unrealistical demands for political autonomy".
"But we have guaranteed them all their rights," he said.

Croatia recently offered a human and minority rights package but the Serbs dismissed it as unsatisfactory, demanding that the area remain a single administrative unit and not be divided into two counties as envisaged by the Croatian constitution.
The mandate of 5,000 U.N. peacekeepers overseeing the reintegration expires on July 15, after which Zagreb wants to take full control of the enclave.
